title: The Pricing Page Is the Hub — the Map of What Needs Doing

intelligence.essence: The pricing page lays out every page and every feature that needs to be completed — it IS the map of what needs doing. Every page shown on it is a page that needs to be completed, with what it does and all its features laid out. That is exactly what the VIEW function tracks: a VIEW button proves the app exists; rows with no view are the apps still to complete.
intelligence.human_view: His framing, in his words: the good thing about this pricing page is it allows you now to have a hub that you can say, hey, here are all the pages that need to be completed. Now I have to have the page to show on this page — so that page needs to be completed. Now you know what needs to be done. You know what it all does, you know all the features, it is all laid out for you. The pricing page is not a sales page; it is the map. The VIEW button is the proof on the map: where there is a view, the app exists; where there is no view, the work is still to do.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine a treasure map that shows every room in a castle, and what is inside each room. The rooms with a little window drawn on them are finished — you can look inside. The rooms with no window are still being built. The map tells you exactly which rooms are left, so nobody has to guess.
intelligence.grandma_view: Think of it like the list on the fridge, dear — every room in the house, and what still needs doing in each one. The pricing page is that list, but for the whole world we are building. Where you can peek inside and see the room, it is done; where there is nothing to peek through, that is the work still waiting. One page, everything laid out, nothing hidden.
intelligence.ai_view: Pricing stops being a page and becomes the hub: the single place where the whole system is visible as a list of apps, each with its features laid out, each either proven by a VIEW button or marked by its absence. The map and the proof are the same object — the VIEW button does not describe the app, it IS the app, live, and its absence is the to-do list. That is why the view-app build (SN-2397) matters as much as any feature: without it the map has no proof, and without the map nobody knows what is left.
intelligence.what_it_means:
- The pricing page is the hub / map: every page shown on it is a page that needs completing, with what it does and all its features laid out.
- The VIEW button is the proof on the map: a row with a view = the app exists; a row without = still to complete.
- A row with no complete app gets NO View button — the button's presence proves the app exists (rule restated to the view-app build seat 23:48Z).
whats_inside:
- The view-app build seat (dispatched 23:48Z, running) carries this rule: wire ONLY real, verified apps — a row with no complete app gets NO View button.
- The pricing page as map belongs in the Factory inventory + brief template when the captain ratifies it (correction compound, rides with LOCK-IN-10 coordinator — flagged, not filed as law by this seat).
- The map is only true if the views are real: a view that opens a mock where a real app was promised would make the map lie. The seat's verification must check that each view opens the real app.
